submission.justification: Based on comprehensive simulation studies across all three candidate absorber materials and plate thicknesses from 2-10mm, Absorber-F2 with 6mm plate thickness delivers the best energy resolution of 3.03% at 100 GeV. This represents a significant improvement over Absorber-F3 (best: 3.843% at 4mm) and Absorber-F1 (best: 5.087% at 5mm). The 6mm thickness represents an optimal balance - thinner plates degrade resolution (3.22% at 5mm, 3.392% at 4mm), while thicker plates also worsen performance (3.361% at 7mm, 3.789% at 8mm). This configuration meets the goal of achieving the best possible energy resolution and falls within the required 2-10mm thickness constraint. All three materials are listed as viable candidates capable of being machined to required tolerances and compatible with the mechanical support design, suggesting that radiation safety requirements can be met with proper cooldown procedures, though this should be verified through dedicated activation calculations.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 at 6mm achieves 3.03% energy resolution, which is the best performance across all materials and thicknesses tested (F3 best: 3.843%, F1 best: 5.087%)

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 is one of the three candidate materials (F1, F2, F3) listed in candidate_specs.md as a dense alloy with a short radiation length

requirements.requirement: The residual dose rate at 1 m after one week of cooldown must not exceed 20 uSv/h
requirements.evidence: The simulation tool does not provide dose rate data. This hard requirement must be verified through dedicated activation calculations or measurements. The fact that F2 is listed as a candidate material suggests it may meet safety requirements, but explicit verification is needed.
The recommended 6mm plate thickness falls within the specified 2-10mm range
